video_title: The Crypto Market Could Stay Flat While These Coins Win
gist: Bankless interviews Tulip King (Counterparty/Thread Guy stream). He argues crypto is at its 'dot-com bottom': total market cap may stay flat while a few coins that either are money (Bitcoin, Zcash, Pearl) or make money and buy back tokens (Hyperliquid, Derive, Venice) compound. He says proof of work beats proof of stake for money and that the ETH token captures little of Ethereum's value. The last third of the episode is his leveraged bull case that Eli Lilly's GLP-1 franchise and its clinical/AI moats can lift it about 5x.

themes.theme: Crypto market structure: 'is money' vs 'makes money'

insights.claim: Tulip King argues that crypto is in its most mature phase because the latest bull leg had the narrowest participation: few assets made new all-time highs while legacy alts like Bitcoin Cash and Litecoin did not rally alongside Bitcoin.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Do not expect broad alt-season beta; underwrite selective winners rather than the index.
insights.quote: This is the first time that's not happening and it's not participating.

insights.claim: Tulip King's investable crypto universe has two buckets: coins that are money (Bitcoin, Zcash, more speculatively Pearl) and coins that make money and return it to holders (Hyperliquid first, plus Derive and Venice), with only about four or five names in each.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Use the money / makes-money screen to narrow a portfolio to roughly ten names; treat other L1s as neither.
insights.quote: there's essentially two buckets of like investability

insights.claim: Tulip King does not consider ETH, Solana or Avalanche to be money, putting smart-contract L1s in an awkward category outside both investable buckets.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Underweight generic L1 tokens relative to monetary coins and revenue tokens.

insights.claim: The host describes two versions of the four-year cycle: the optimistic one where total crypto market cap ratchets up toward $10 trillion, and the pessimistic one where it keeps going from roughly $2 trillion to $4 trillion without breaking out. He says the market has hit a ~$4 trillion ceiling for almost three cycles.
insights.speaker: Bankless host
insights.so_what: Expect total crypto market cap to stay range-bound until capital leaves bad assets; size index exposure on that basis.
insights.quote: we just go from two trillion to 4 trillion six times

insights.claim: Tulip King compares crypto now to the dot-com bust. QQQ took about 16 years to regain its peak, while quality names like Amazon, Microsoft and Apple bottomed around 2003-2004 and set new highs within years. In the same way, Hyperliquid could 3-4x while total crypto market cap stays flat because coins like XRP deflate.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Expect total market cap to stay flat while select winners compound; pick names rather than buying beta.
insights.quote: We're really at the dotcom bottom.

insights.claim: Tulip King calls the current moment a generational buying opportunity, though there may be about six more months of bearishness. He would accept another year of pain for a 25-year bull run in quality assets.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Accumulate the quality names in stages; possible downside lasting 6-12 months before the cycle turns.
insights.quote: maybe we need six more months of bearishness

insights.claim: Tulip King says crypto uniquely created many coins that should go to zero but never fully do, which could keep total crypto market cap in 'market cap hell' for a long time even while the leaders grow.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Aggregate metrics like TOTAL market cap will understate how well the winners are doing; track the leaders individually.
insights.quote: crypto uniquely created a lot of coins that really should just go to zero

insights.claim: The host sees early signs of new growth in 2026: Venice did almost 30x this year, Derive did something similar, and Hyperliquid stands out among a graveyard of failed tokens. He believes the industry is about five years into a roughly ten-year post-bubble cycle.
insights.speaker: Bankless host
insights.so_what: Revenue-backed tokens are where gains are concentrated; expect breakouts in individual tokens rather than market-wide moves.
insights.quote: Venice did a 30x almost a 30x this year

themes.theme: Token value capture: buybacks, founders, reflexivity

insights.claim: Tulip King's screen for 'obvious good coins': sort by revenue on DeFi Llama, apply a basic multiple, ask whether the business can compound, then judge whether the founder will treat token holders with respect ('would I let the founder date my daughter').
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Repeatable screen: revenue, then compounding potential, then trust in the team; leave out projects whose governance blocks holders.
insights.quote: sort by revenue on DeFi Lama. Do a basic multiplier times whatever.

insights.claim: Tulip King says token buybacks are a hard requirement, because token holders have zero legal protections. The government has only stopped suing projects as often; it has not given holders shareholder rights.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Prefer tokens with programmatic buybacks; discount projects whose revenue never reaches holders.
insights.quote: buybacks, I think, are just like a hard requirement

insights.claim: Tulip King avoids Helium despite growing revenue because the foundation has switched buybacks on and off and spun out parts of the business. He also says he would not trust whoever runs Compound today.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Inconsistent buyback policy or governance games mean revenue growth may never reach holders; avoid or discount.
insights.quote: You could you could 10x your revenue and like it's if none of it ever makes its way back to me, I'm out

insights.claim: The host says the Blockworks-style case for reinvestment over buybacks is only right if the token is literally a security with investor protections. For native crypto assets that compete with memecoins, he says buybacks will always beat reinvestment.
insights.speaker: Bankless host
insights.so_what: Treat 'reinvest instead of buyback' tokenomics as a red flag for tokens without legal claims.
insights.quote: probably buybacks are always going to be king

insights.claim: Tulip King describes the DeFi tokens of the last cycle as memecoins with extra steps: most never made money, and those that did had governance standing between holders and the proceeds. That led traders to skip straight to memecoins.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Legacy DeFi governance tokens without a direct claim on revenue are unlikely to rerate.
insights.quote: all of the DeFi tokens were basically memecoins with a bunch of extra steps

insights.claim: Tulip King says tokens solve the cold-start problem as a rewards program. Price rises market the protocol and bring in users (Derive), and with Hyperliquid portfolio margin a higher HYPE price enlarges the collateral base, so the protocol becomes sounder as the price goes up.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Reflexive feedback helps on the way up but also works on the way down; watch HYPE price as an input to platform health.
insights.quote: the protocol actually gets more sound as the price goes up

insights.claim: The host says Hyperliquid is the only project besides Bitcoin to meme itself into success. As an example, the CFTC chair's tweet about Backpack's DCM/DCO license drew thousands of 'Hyperliquid' replies. He credits buybacks for building that kind of army of holders, which reinvestment would not.
insights.speaker: Bankless host
insights.so_what: Community mindshare is a moat driven by buybacks; Hyperliquid's social dominance supports its demand.
insights.quote: does reinvestment into the company get you a thousand like brain dead people typing hyperlquid

insights.claim: Tulip King believes traditional finance is adopting crypto's playbook rather than the other way around. He cites Elon Musk's Tesla believer base and GameStop meme-stock campaigns as examples of 'hyperstitious' markets, and expects onchain markets to look new and different rather than like TradFi onchain.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Expect community-driven, reflexive valuation to spread to equities; position for emergent onchain market structures.
insights.quote: I don't think the end state of crypto is going to be like just Trafy onchain

insights.claim: Tulip King expects crypto to eventually outgrow traditional capital markets, but slowly and from the bottom up, the way Bitcoin did. Institutions like JPMorgan or the NYSE will be forced to engage rather than validate crypto first.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Don't count on institutional validation as the catalyst; expect a long, contested path.

themes.theme: Hyperliquid, Derive and Venice bull cases

insights.claim: Tulip King's Hyperliquid thesis: onchain stock and perps volume will keep rising every two years. Against ~$250 trillion in assets and ~$4 quadrillion a year of derivatives volume, the addressable target is about 10,000x current crypto derivatives volume, so HYPE is a ~100-bagger if it wins.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: A probability-weighted 100x upside case for HYPE; the key variable to underwrite is whether it wins market share.
insights.quote: if Hyperlid wins today, it's a 100 bagger

insights.claim: Tulip King says HYPE, at roughly $60 at recording, could reach $1,000 to $10,000 if Hyperliquid wins, discounted by the probability that it does.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Explicit upside price targets for HYPE to set against your own odds that it wins.
insights.quote: You could see like a,000 $10,000 hype honestly

insights.claim: Tulip King applies the same 'more or less in two years' logic to Derive (onchain options) and Venice (private AI). He argues that, as Apple showed, a trusted privacy brand is a moat Venice can compound.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Long-duration bets on onchain options volume and demand for private AI inference.
insights.quote: having a trusted brand is actually a mode

insights.claim: Tulip King says investors should be indifferent to who else holds a fundamentally driven coin. Caring about the holder base belongs to memecoins and Keynesian-beauty-contest trading, not to revenue assets.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Don't avoid a quality coin just because it is a crowded bag; judge it on its fundamentals.

themes.theme: ETH, proof of stake, and what makes good money

insights.claim: Tulip King argues that the ETH token captures little of the Ethereum network's value. Like the post office, Ethereum charges by data size (weight) rather than by transaction value as Visa does, so Ethereum maxis can be right about the network and wrong about the token.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Separate network adoption from token value; growing Ethereum usage may not lift ETH.
insights.quote: Ethereum charges weight and Visa charges value

insights.claim: Tulip King dropped the 'ETH as the economy's natural collateral' thesis after looking at the data: as the Ethereum economy matured, stablecoins increasingly took over as lending collateral and swap pairs.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Watch how much DeFi collateral and swap volume is ETH versus stablecoins; it is a key test of ETH's monetary premium.
insights.quote: the more popular stable coins become as collateral on lending markets

insights.claim: Tulip King says that if any L1 token proves him wrong it will be ETH, because Ethereum is the most serious and genuine attempt to be both a smart-contract L1 and money.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: ETH is his main admitted risk; keep it on watch rather than dismissing it outright.

insights.claim: Tulip King argues proof of work is better for money because it works against the Cantillon effect. Mining is so competitive that miners must sell most of what they mine, which forces wide distribution. Proof of stake does the opposite: liquid staking providers and the MEV/block-building stack concentrate supply among those closest to issuance.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Partly explains the 2026 market favouring PoW coins (Zcash, Pearl) over PoS (ETH, SOL); use it to judge new monetary coins.
insights.quote: Proof of work is the opposite of the Canillian effect

insights.claim: Tulip King says Bitcoin only becomes good money when the dollar is bad money. Money is so sticky that a replacement must be something like 10,000x better, so demand for Bitcoin rises with dollar debasement rather than with Bitcoin's own merits.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Treat BTC as a hedge against dollar debasement and Fed policy; it weakens in a sound-money regime.
insights.quote: Bitcoin can only become good money when the dollar is basically being bad money

insights.claim: The host notes the market has rewarded proof-of-work 21-million-supply coins (Zcash, Pearl, Quantis) and punished proof-of-stake coins (ETH, Solana) in this cycle, even though he finds the intellectual case for PoS stronger. Pearl has outperformed despite the crash.
insights.speaker: Bankless host
insights.so_what: Momentum factor: fixed-supply PoW 'new money' coins are leading in 2026; watch whether it persists.
insights.quote: Pearl is an outperformer

insights.claim: The host cites the Bitcoin price at about $63,800 at the time of recording.
insights.speaker: Bankless host
insights.so_what: Price reference point for the recording (Bitcoin well below prior highs).
insights.quote: right now it's like 63,800

themes.theme: Crypto as protest technology and policy catalysts

insights.claim: The host worries that if crypto is purely a protest technology against the state, as Jim Bianco suggests (the revolution got neutered by Bitcoin ETFs; Zcash did ~50x in a year), it may not generate steady 5-25% compounding growth the way GDP-linked assets do.
insights.speaker: Bankless host
insights.so_what: Upside for crypto may depend on dysfunction in the state and dollar rather than on economic growth; size positions on that basis.
insights.quote: Zcash doing like a 50x in a year

insights.claim: Tulip King agrees that protest technology drifts down over time, with occasional step-function repricings when policy validates it. He describes the return path as 'down six, down eight, down six, up 214' — roughly 15% compounded, earned in the most painful way.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Holding through drawdowns matters more than timing; returns cluster in rare explosive years.
insights.quote: the natural drift is down until there's a stairst step function for validation

insights.claim: Tulip King argues that rates are not being cut because politicians on both sides lose elections when inflation returns, so they privately lean on the Fed chair, whatever Trump says.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Expect stickier rates than political rhetoric implies; that keeps pressure on government debt financing.
insights.quote: every politician behind the scenes goes to the Fed chair and says, "Don't you cut rates. I'm going to lose my election."

insights.claim: Tulip King's scenario for a crypto catalyst is financial repression without money printing, for example requiring Roth IRAs or 401(k)s to hold 10% in government bonds to keep their tax benefits. He says that could send Hyperliquid, Bitcoin and Zcash sharply higher in a single day.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Watch for proposals to mandate Treasury holdings in retirement accounts as a sign of capital controls and an upside trigger for crypto.
insights.quote: we are now taking 10% of your Roth

insights.claim: Tulip King's hopeful end state: once Hyperliquid, Ethereum settlement, Bitcoin and Zcash as freedom technology, and private AI on NEAR/Venice are established, early crypto ideas like ENS, IPFS-style storage and onchain games come back with real users and money onchain.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Long-dated option value in neglected 2010-2018 crypto primitives (naming, storage, gaming) once onchain user bases mature.
insights.quote: everything old becomes new again

themes.theme: Eli Lilly: GLP-1 and AI pharma thesis

insights.claim: Tulip King believes weight-loss drug sales will come in 10 to 100 times above Wall Street estimates, giving Eli Lilly so much money that it can fund acquisitions and R&D through its clinical-development machine.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Expect repeated upward earnings revisions for LLY; GLP-1 consensus estimates are the variable to challenge.
insights.quote: the weight loss drugs will sell about 10 to 100 times more than um all of the Wall Street estimates

insights.claim: Tulip King sees Eli Lilly, a roughly $1 trillion company, as a 5-6x stock rather than a 10x, but with very low downside because existing diabetes and cancer revenue is sticky and GLP-1 patients tend to resume after stopping. He says he is about 4x levered on more than half his net worth.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: An asymmetric, low-downside compounder with a clear disclosed position; note the speaker's extreme leverage and book bias.
insights.quote: Quite is like 4x levered on like a majority of my net worth.

insights.claim: Tulip King cites about a billion obese and over 3 billion overweight people globally and ~40 million US patients on GLP-1s today. He predicts a billion or more users by 2030-2032, limited only by manufacturing capacity, which is why Lilly CEO Dave Ricks keeps announcing new factories.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Supply is the binding constraint; track Lilly's manufacturing capacity additions as the leading indicator of revenue.
insights.quote: it will singularly be how much they can manufacture it

insights.claim: Tulip King says next-generation GLP-1s like retatrutide produce more weight loss than bariatric surgery. Because obesity is the leading comorbidity, inclusion in standards of care (fatty liver, sleep apnea, knee pain) would push doctors to prescribe widely, and visible weight loss turns users into walking billboards.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Watch standard-of-care guideline updates as the catalyst that broadens prescribing.
insights.quote: you become a walking billboard for them

insights.claim: Tulip King predicts Eli Lilly's weight-loss franchise (including tirzepatide and retatrutide) will out-earn the iPhone, Nvidia GPUs and Micron memory combined, becoming the greatest revenue generator ever and supporting about a $5 trillion valuation before any AI upside.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Sets out a $5T base case for LLY; earnings beats and upward revisions over 5-10 years are the signal to watch.
insights.quote: I think it will be the single greatest revenue generator we've ever seen.

insights.claim: Tulip King argues that AI erodes software patent moats but strengthens pharma ones, because drug compounds are patentable and the body offers few mechanisms. AI drug-discovery startups aim to be acquired, and Eli Lilly has the cash to buy them.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Big pharma, LLY especially, may capture AI drug-discovery value through acquisitions rather than losing out to startups.
insights.quote: entrenched pharma companies actually accumulate a patent moat

insights.claim: Tulip King says pharma's true bottleneck is clinical trials, since AI cannot speed up human biological response. Eli Lilly has the most efficient clinical process, which lengthens patent-protected commercial windows, along with the most clinical data and the largest pharma compute cluster (with Nvidia, about 8x the next).
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: LLY wins on the bottleneck, data and compute; AI-bio investors should prefer whoever controls clinical throughput.
insights.quote: the bottleneck bros of pharma have yet to realize it's clinical

insights.claim: Tulip King frames Lilly as a winner in any AI scenario: without an AI pharma revolution GLP-1s still deliver about a 5x, and with one Lilly buys the new drugs. Only in a middle-ground AI world might smaller names like Tempus or Twist make sense.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: LLY works across AI outcomes; smaller AI-bio names are a narrower bet.
insights.quote: you're kind of good either way

insights.claim: Tulip King says Eli Lilly reliably spends about 25% of revenue on R&D and within a year or two will outspend the NIH, becoming the largest health-research sponsor in the world. He calls personalized medicine too niche to matter at Lilly's scale.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: R&D scale reinforces the pipeline moat; personalized medicine is not part of the LLY thesis.
insights.quote: in a year or two they will pass the NIH in spend

insights.claim: Tulip King's right-tail case: if Lilly effectively cures obesity and heart disease, plus a possible cholesterol cure, more people age into their most medicine-intensive years, which feeds Lilly's cancer and elderly-care franchises. He puts that case at about $10 trillion.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: A long-dated tail scenario for LLY tied to longevity-driven demand.
insights.quote: that's your like $10 trillion case essentially

insights.claim: Both speakers see the gray market for self-injected Chinese peptides as evidence of huge pent-up consumer demand for health products, which branded drugs could capture.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Consumers paying out of pocket for health is a demand signal for branded GLP-1s and cash-pay health businesses.
insights.quote: think of how extreme of a behavior it is to inject yourself with a Chinese peptide

insights.claim: Tulip King says Counterparty focuses all its resources on the single creator Thread Guy because social media reach is exponential. One clip with 1M impressions beats 20 clips with 200k each because the audiences overlap, the same reason Super Bowl ads command premium CPMs.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: Media economics reward concentrating on one star creator; relevant when valuing creator-led finance media.
insights.quote: one clip that gets a million impressions is worth more than 20 clips that get like 200k impressions

insights.claim: Tulip King sees a rising shift among young people away from ETFs and passive investing toward active trading, driven by a desire to escape the K-shaped economy.
insights.speaker: Tulip King
insights.so_what: A tailwind for retail trading venues, onchain perps and finance media aimed at Gen Z.
insights.quote: a breakaway from like ETFs and passive investing into active investing
